LORD SALES · UK SUPREME COURT · NOV 2026 Human in the loop, or human rubber stamp? The deputy president of the UK Supreme Court says AI may one day decide small cases. India's Supreme Court has drafted a ban. Both are worried about the same thing: lawyers and judges who stop thinking. AI in courts Automation bias Junior lawyers Adv. Ashwani Kumar · Advocate | Data Privacy & Technology Law 01 / 08

WHAT LORD SALES SAID AI could decide some cases “For low-value civil disputes, we may eventually accept forms of automated determination, particularly where parties agree.” Lord Sales, Deputy President, UK Supreme Court 1 Why: courts face a “tsunami” of claims written and filed by people using AI. “AI may itself have to be enlisted by the courts to become part of the solution.” 2 How far: mainly simpler cases, with AI making initial decisions that a human can review. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 02 / 08

THE REAL WARNING The danger isn't only wrong answers “The ‘human in the loop’ can gradually become the human rubber stamp.” Lord Sales He described automation bias as “the tendency to accept the machine's answer precisely because the machine usually gets things right.” “The greater long-term danger is that human beings gradually lose the ability to know whether it has got the answer wrong.” A judge who stops researching, analysing and writing loses the skill needed to check the machine. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 03 / 08

JUNIOR LAWYERS Who trains tomorrow's senior lawyer? “The less efficient human process has been producing two different things at once: today's legal work and tomorrow's lawyer.” Lord Sales, speaking at a conference in London WHAT A FIRM GAINS NOW WHAT IT MAY LOSE LATER Research and first drafts Juniors who learn by in seconds doing the work Fewer junior hours billed Seniors able to spot what “May improve its AI got wrong productivity this year” “Where does the experienced senior lawyer come from?” Adv. INDIA'S POSITION Our courts have drawn a harder line Jul 2025 · Kerala HC First AI policy for the district judiciary: AI tools must not be used to arrive at findings, reliefs, orders or judgments. Only approved tools; ChatGPT-type tools barred. Jun 2026 · Supreme Court The SC's AI Committee publishes draft Regulations for Use of AI in Courts, 2026: a complete ban on AI deciding judicial outcomes, built on “human primacy”. Consultation closed 15 July. 2026 · CJI Surya Kant AI can help with research and managing work, but judgment and decision-making must stay with judges. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 05 / 08

SIDE BY SIDE Two systems, one shared fear UK · LORD SALES' VIEW INDIA · SC DRAFT RULES Open to automated No AI-decided outcomes, decisions in low-value in any case civil disputes AI allowed for research, Especially where both drafting, translation, parties agree transcription, case AI decides first; a human management can review Lawyers must disclose AI-assisted filings Where they agree: a human must stay genuinely in charge, and able to tell when the machine is wrong. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 06 / 08

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR US How not to become the rubber stamp 1 Keep doing some work the slow way. Draft a few pleadings and research notes yourself. That is how judgment is built. 2 Read AI output like the other side's draft. Look for what is wrong, missing or invented. 3 Verify every citation and quotation against the official report before it goes into a filing. 4 Expect to disclose AI use. The SC's draft rules would require it for court filings. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 07 / 08

MY TAKE Speed is useful. Judgment is the job. India is right to keep AI out of deciding cases for now. But a ban on AI verdicts does not stop the quieter risk Lord Sales describes: lawyers and judges who accept a machine's draft because it is usually right. Would you accept an AI decision in a small claim if both sides agreed? Adv.
